A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Planning and Learning in Average Risk-aware MDPs. All 37 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original convergence simulations, algorithm comparisons and machine replacement, water reservoir and inventory management experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and reports revised soft-quantile convergence curves in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The RVI/RQI updates, MLMC estimator and synchronous/asynchronous UBSR Q-learning procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A. The revised experimental soft-quantile parameter uses the existing loss definition.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same generated MDPs and machine replacement, water reservoir and inventory management tasks. The soft-quantile revision changes a configuration within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparison methods: value iteration, risk-aware RVI, MLMC Q-learning and synchronous/asynchronous UBSR Q-learning. The application comparisons retain the same risk-aware and risk-neutral policies.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the reported soft-quantile setting from κ = 1 to κ = 2 for both synchronous and asynchronous convergence experiments, retaining α = 0.2. The stated MDP generation, step sizes and iteration budgets remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether this reflects rerunning or correcting prior reporting.

E4.justification: The supplementary tests of UBSR convergence under soft-quantile losses are revised in Figures C.1 and C.2. The polynomial mixed-utility tests, MLMC sampling sensitivity, expectile sensitivity and application policy analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged, including 100-run experiments, 5th/95th percentile bands and tabulated standard deviations. The revised soft-quantile bands change reported results, not the uncertainty estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The soft-quantile panels of Figures C.1 and C.2 contain different convergence trajectories and percentile bands for κ = 2. Both versions show convergence toward the reference optimum; the changed setting prevents interpreting the differences as same-setting performance gains. Tables 5.1, C.1 and C.2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theorem conclusions and Appendix B proofs retain their mathematical substance. Theorem 4.5 makes the already implicit state dependence of the greedy action explicit, and Lemma B.3 standardizes 'span-seminorm fixed point' terminology.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: risk-aware RVI planning, MLMC and UBSR learning algorithms, proven RVI/MLMC convergence and empirical support for UBSR convergence.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the unconditional characterization of both loss functions as neither convex nor concave to 'generally' having this property, allowing parameter-dependent exceptions. Interpretations of convergence and the unresolved theoretical convergence of UBSR remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 revises the documented soft-quantile hyperparameter from κ = 1 to κ = 2 in both experiment descriptions. Other implementation information, including Python 3.9 and the Linux server with an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to risk-neutral, entropic-risk and distributionally robust MDP research remain unchanged. Citation punctuation edits introduce no new research relationship.

P1.justification: Scattered grammar, terminology, punctuation and equation-reference edits occur throughout the main text and proofs, including 'Taking minimum' and consistent 'average risk-aware' wording. Section order and narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The soft-quantile panels in Figures C.1 and C.2 are redrawn and relabeled κ = 2, while their polynomial mixed-utility panels remain identical. Minor caption edits and local text reflow accompany otherwise unchanged figure, table and page organization.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.2 becomes more internally consistent: with α = 0.2, the printed loss at v2's κ = 1 is concave, contrary to its description. v3 uses κ = 2, for which the loss is neither convex nor concave, updates the convergence plots and qualifies the characterization. This improves the relevance and accuracy of the supplementary example, while the central contributions and remaining evidence stay unchanged.
